title: Atlantic voyagers · around 1000
question: Which archaeological site preserves evidence of a Norse settlement in Newfoundland?
explanation: Norse seafarers established a short-lived base at L’Anse aux Meadows around the year 1000. This is evidence of a European presence, not the beginning of Indigenous history.

title: A St. Lawrence foothold
question: Which French explorer founded the colonial settlement at Québec in 1608?
explanation: Samuel de Champlain founded Québec in 1608. The French fur trade depended on Indigenous traders and intermediaries, including the Montagnais, Algonquin and Huron First Nations.

title: Rights and the Crown
question: The Royal Proclamation became a foundation for which process?
explanation: Issued on October 7, 1763, the Royal Proclamation established procedures concerning First Nations lands and helped form a basis for treaty-making and the relationship with the Crown.

title: A federation takes shape
question: Which four provinces formed the federation in 1867?

options.text: Ontario, Québec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick
Manitoba, Alberta, Saskatchewan and British Columbia
Newfoundland, Prince Edward Island, Ontario and Yukon

explanation: Confederation brought Ontario, Québec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick together in 1867. Full independence from Britain developed through later constitutional changes.

title: Red River negotiations
question: Which Métis leader headed the provisional government involved in the creation of Manitoba?
explanation: Louis Riel led a provisional government at Red River. Negotiations between its representatives and the federal government produced the Manitoba Act, and Manitoba joined Confederation in 1870.

title: An unequal colonial law
question: Under the original Indian Act, who could lose registered status by marrying a man without Indian status?
explanation: The Indian Act was enacted in 1876. Its discriminatory marriage rules removed status from First Nations women who married men without status, while men retained status regardless of marriage. Later amendments sought to address these inequities.

title: The last spike
question: In which province was the Canadian Pacific Railway’s ceremonial last spike driven?
explanation: Donald Smith drove the ceremonial last spike at Craigellachie in British Columbia on November 7, 1885, marking completion of the Canadian Pacific Railway.

source.title: Library and Archives Canada: Last spike

title: Vimy Ridge · overseas
question: In which country did Canadian troops fight the Battle of Vimy Ridge?
explanation: The Battle of Vimy Ridge took place in northern France from April 9 to 12, 1917, during the First World War. Its capture came at a heavy human cost.

title: The Persons Case
question: What did the 1929 Persons Case establish about women’s eligibility?

options.text: They could join Confederation as a province
They alone could vote in every election
They were eligible for appointment to the Senate

explanation: The Famous Five won the Persons Case in 1929. The ruling recognized women as persons for the constitutional provision governing appointment to the Senate; it did not instantly remove every barrier to equality.

title: A new national symbol
question: Which symbol is at the centre of the national flag first raised in 1965?
explanation: The red-and-white maple leaf flag was first raised on Parliament Hill on February 15, 1965. The maple leaf was already a familiar symbol before the new flag was adopted.

title: Rights in the Constitution
question: Which document became part of the Constitution in 1982?

options.text: The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms

explanation: The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms came into force on April 17, 1982. Its equality-rights section took effect three years later, in 1985.

title: Our land
question: What does Nunavut mean in Inuktitut?
explanation: Nunavut means “our land” in Inuktitut. The territory was created on April 1, 1999, following a process tied to the Inuit land claims agreement.
